text:
laura: incident-bot: page fired — pd_incident: capacity_queue_high in us-west-2-inference :rotating_light:
pd-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered (P1): Capacity queue backlog > 10k (service: inference-queue). Pager: @michael @laura
michael: acked on PD, I'm on it. Quick snapshot: queue_depth ~20,123, active_instances=18, pending_provision=0, p50 latency=120ms, p95=1.4s, p99=3.8s
laura: any 5xx/429 spike metrics? customer-facing impact?
sam: support triage: 429s on /v1/generate climbed to ~4% for a handful of heavy tenants. Support ticket OPS-7891 created and linked to this thread
ingrid: digging into provisioning logs — autoscaler attempted node creates but cloud API returned 429 RateLimitExceeded on instance create. Looks like provider-side create throttle
sre-bot: Metric snapshot @1717067890: queue_depth=20123, inflight_requests=4520, active_pods=120, active_instances=18, pending_node_creates=0
michael: confirmed. No pending nodes are being created (request rejected by provider). Kube events show repeated create failures, backoff kicking in
laura: mitigation options: 1) manual console spin-up (requires admin creds), 2) enable burst-pool/prewarmed instances, 3) apply traffic shaping/circuit breaker for non-critical tenants, 4) route heavy customers to smaller/fallback model to reduce tokens
sam: I'll try manual spin-up from console. @michael can you prepare routing changes?
michael: starting routing changes — will flip A/B flag for non-critical tenants to fallback model `redwood-mini-v2` and temporarily lower route weight for realtime-high routes
ingrid: manual API spin-up attempt returns same 429 on the cloud API, so manual create via API blocked too. Console UI create currently rate-limited as well
laura: ok manual create blocked. Next, try enabling burst pool via internal admin ops API (runbook allows burst-enable for emergencies)
michael: issuing admin call to enable burst pool for us-west-2: `curl -X POST "https://internal-admin/api/ops/enable_burst?region=us-west-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"` — CALL RETURNED 200, burst_scale +10 nodes queued
sre-bot: Event: burst_pool_scale_up started (expected join ~90s)
sam: patching autoscaler worker concurrency to reduce per-node load to lower queue build-up: applying `MAX_CONCURRENCY=40` per worker to force more vertical pods
laura: good. Also bumping scheduler preemption window and reducing batcher window to degrade tail latency gracefully
michael: routing change applied: non-critical tenants -> `redwood-mini-v2` fallback, route weight lowered for heavy realtime routes. Early telemetry: p95 latency dropping to ~1.6s; queue depth trending down 20k -> 13k
ingrid: provider confirmed we hit account-level instance create throttle; opened support case with provider (SR-442332). They estimate lift in 5–10 minutes if quota resets; escalated to partner channel
pd-bot: PagerDuty: Acknowledged by michael
sam: posting short customer impact blurb to ops-status channel and tagging growth/support: "Partial degradation: elevated latency and increased 429 for some tenants; mitigation applied: routing fallback and burst enable. No full-service outage."
laura: customer impact summary (for incident page): 3% 429 rate on generation API for ~6 tenants, embeddings experiencing high latency; payments/critical infrastructure unaffected. SLA violations likely for a few enterprise customers if not resolved within 30m
michael: adding to incident board with actions; monitoring in progress — will watch queue drop below 2k as recovery target
ingrid: burst nodes are joining the fleet, new instances coming up (observed 6/10 joined). Pending join delays due to node bootstrap (kubelet + kv-cache warmup)
sre-bot: Metric update @1717068250: queue_depth=9200, active_instances=26, pending_boot=4, avg_queue_time=42s
sam: 429 rate down to 1.1%, p99 now 2.4s. Good progress but still elevated
laura: notes on what we tried: - manual creates blocked by provider rate limit - enabled burst pool via admin API - patched autoscaler concurrency down - applied fallback routing to smaller model
michael: leaving notes for next on-call: if provider doesn't lift create throttle within 30m do: 1) escalate with provider support (we have partner channel), 2) enable region-wide heavy-tenant pre-warm for next 24h, 3) consider temporary capacity reserve purchase
sam: documenting commands used (for runbook and postmortem):
```
kubectl patch deploy inference --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"server","env":[{"name":"MAX_CONCURRENCY","value":"40"}]}}]}}}'
curl -X POST "https://internal-admin/api/ops/enable_burst?region=us-west-2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
# routing toggle
curl -X POST "https://internal-config/api/routes/set?service=embeddings&fallback=redwood-mini-v2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CONFIG_TOKEN"
```
michael: monitoring dashboard: https://internal-grafana/d/inf/queue-depth?orgId=1&from=now-1h to=now — updating incident board https://z/incidents/1717067890
pd-bot: PagerDuty: Incident still open — no resolve event
sam: queue ~9.2k now, p99 2.1s, 429 ~0.9% — trending down steadily
ingrid: I'll take watch for the next hour. If recovery stalls I will escalate to ENG-SRE L2. Runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/autoscaler-rate-limit
laura: agreed. Action items to capture: [1] provider quota request + partner escalation, [2] add automated pre-warm for top 50 tenants, [3] implement fallback routing as permanent safety valve, [4] postmortem within 48h with token-level cost/regression analysis
michael: assigning owners on the incident board; will follow up with a short internal email to affected account managers
laura: handing off to next on-call @ingrid — full details in incident board and runbook. Thanks everyone.
ingrid: taking over handoff — ack :thumbsup: keeping 1hr watch, will escalate per runbook if provider quota not lifted by 19:15 UTC
